nodes.label: SEC EDGAR + USAspending
nodes.subtitle: Public filings and 78K+ federal awards — every number has a provenance trail

evidence.text: Seed data carries EDGAR provenance links; federal contracts are the substance signal.

nodes.whyItMatters: Provenance beats name shape: a node is judged by where its facts came from, and these are the sources.
questions: Which source would you add next, and what new failure modes does it import?

nodes.label: Extraction flywheel
nodes.subtitle: LLM agents propose typed facts; throughput lives here, truth does not

evidence.text: 1,083 pending supply-edge drafts imported from the live queue, contributor 'mithrandir'.

nodes.whyItMatters: The division of labor: agents draft and cross-examine, deterministic code verifies, humans own publication.
questions: What is the flywheel's precision at the gate, per failure mode, per month?

nodes.label: Citation-check agents
nodes.subtitle: Independent adjudicators that see only the proposal and its source

evidence.text: manage.py citation_check regenerates summaries live when an API key is set; seeds ship precomputed.

nodes.whyItMatters: Independence is the point: the checker never sees the extractor's reasoning, so agreement means something.
questions: Should citation checks gate imports, or stay advisory to the human?
nodes.undrawnRelation: AUDITS the flywheel — drawn as advice, not as an edge.

nodes.label: Draft queues
nodes.subtitle: Edges, retypes, merges — pending, named, and none of it published

evidence.text: EdgeProposal / TypeProposal / MergeProposal rows imported read-only from the live graph.

nodes.whyItMatters: Absence is honest: a draft is a claim awaiting judgment, structurally unable to masquerade as a fact.
questions: What's the queue's aging profile — does anything rot un-adjudicated?

nodes.label: Astraea.Gate (.NET 8)
nodes.subtitle: Reconciliation + ontology law; verdicts are named, never lumped

evidence.text: First live run: 1,083 edges pass; 14 of 20 retypes refused as substance_demotion (~$10.9B protected).

nodes.whyItMatters: Deterministic validation wants a compiler: typed law that refuses provable errors and names each refusal.
questions: Which rule earns the next slot — stale references, or unit-scale checks?

nodes.label: Named failure modes
nodes.subtitle: undetected_rollup, bare_name_merge, substance_demotion…

evidence.text: Every gate verdict is a named mode with a definition; 'failed' is not a verdict.

nodes.whyItMatters: A named failure can be triaged, counted, and argued with; an unnamed one is just a shrug.
questions: Which failure mode fires most in production, and is that a bug in the data or the rule?

nodes.label: Adjudication portal (Django 5)
nodes.subtitle: Review queues with refusal built into the approve button

evidence.text: Approving an unreconciled proposal returns a hard refusal in the admin and HTTP 409 on the API.

nodes.whyItMatters: Human-in-the-loop curation is a CRUD-and-permissions problem; Django's admin is the best such machine ever shipped.
questions: What does reviewer throughput look like, and where does the UI waste their judgment?

nodes.label: The human curator
nodes.subtitle: Owns publication; judges what the gate cannot prove

evidence.text: The gate is a floor, not a verdict: contract-less judgment calls (The MathWorks) route to a person.

nodes.whyItMatters: AI is load-bearing for throughput, never for truth — someone accountable clicks approve.
questions: What evidence would let a reviewer overrule a gate refusal, if anything?

nodes.label: A wrong number is worse than no number
nodes.subtitle: Nothing publishes unless it reconciles

evidence.text: The repo's founding rule: absence is honest; a plausible wrong figure is undetectable downstream.

nodes.whyItMatters: Every architectural choice above bends around this one constraint; remove it and the system is just plumbing.
questions: Where would you accept a confidence-weighted publish, if anywhere?

nodes.label: The knowledge graph
nodes.subtitle: space_kg.db — ~34K organizations, typed edges, opened read-only here

evidence.text: Connector opens SQLite in mode=ro; substance is counted across the full NODE_REF_COLS mirror.

nodes.whyItMatters: Astraea never writes it: decisions export as a JSON log for the graph's own dry-run-by-default sweeps.
questions: When does the decisions log become a two-way sync, and what gates that?

nodes.label: Ontology census
nodes.subtitle: Node types, relation types, and ref-columns enumerated from the schema

evidence.text: 14 node types and 10 relation types captured live, with per-table reference columns.

nodes.whyItMatters: Hand-written schema lists drift — the census is enumerated from sqlite_master because drift once cost $134.7B in miscounted orphans.
questions: Should the census diff itself between imports and flag schema drift loudly?

nodes.label: Substance stats
nodes.subtitle: Live edges + federal contracts + identity bridges, per node

evidence.text: The signal that refused 14 demotions: The Aerospace Corporation holds 213 contracts ($9.1B).

nodes.whyItMatters: Provenance beats name shape, operationalized: nodes are judged by what they hold, not how they read.
questions: What belongs in substance next — news mentions, ownership filings, or nothing?

nodes.label: This viewer
nodes.subtitle: React 18 — lanes, typed edges, dossiers; the graph.json contract is generic

evidence.text: You are looking at the sample instance; pass ?graph=<name> to load another.

nodes.whyItMatters: The rendering layer knows nothing about any company — the contract is the product.
questions: What second instance earns the build — a customer-facing one, or an internal architecture map?

operatingThesis.title: Truth is a service with an API
operatingThesis.body: The reconciliation and identity rules aren't documentation — they're a typed service other systems must call. A rule you can't invoke is a rule that erodes.
operatingThesis.sayItAs: Say it as: the CLAUDE.md rulebook, compiled.

operatingThesis.title: AI proposes, humans dispose
operatingThesis.body: Agents generate throughput no human team could match, and exactly zero of it publishes without a deterministic verdict and a human click.
operatingThesis.sayItAs: Say it as: load-bearing for throughput, never for truth.

operatingThesis.title: Judge nodes by what they hold
operatingThesis.body: Name-shape heuristics wanted to demote The Aerospace Corporation. Substance stats — contracts, edges, identity bridges — refused, fourteen times in one run.
operatingThesis.sayItAs: Say it as: provenance beats name shape, in production.

operatingThesis.title: Read-only is a feature
operatingThesis.body: Astraea holds no write path to the graph. Decisions leave as a JSON log for governed, reversible sweeps — the blast radius of a bad day is a file.
operatingThesis.sayItAs: Say it as: the apply step is someone else's dry run.

shortlistQuestions.question: Which ontology rule should earn the next slot in the gate, and what real incident justifies it?
What is the aging profile of the pending queues — does anything rot un-adjudicated?
What evidence, if any, should let a reviewer overrule a gate refusal?
When does the decisions log become a two-way sync, and what has to be true first?
Should independent citation checks gate imports, or stay advisory?
What second graph instance earns the build?
